questions.prompt: How does TypeScript commonly decide whether object types are compatible?
options: Compatibility is decided by checking the database schema at runtime.
Structural compatibility: the value must provide the required members with compatible types.
Only the interface and class names are compared.
Objects are compatible only if constructed by the same factory.
questions.answer_key: Structural compatibility: the value must provide the required members with compatible types.
questions.explanation: TypeScript is largely structurally typed; specialized patterns such as branding add explicit distinctions.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Introduction to Interfaces”?
options: The concept should be demonstrated with declaring object contracts and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with declaring object contracts and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Declaring object contracts”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Introduction to Interfaces”?
options: Assume implementing interface contracts is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check required and optional members, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Check required and optional members, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Required and optional members”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
